title: Topic 1 · 感知即推断 — 神经科学

questions.question: 按预测加工的框架，「注意」到底在做什么？
options: 关闭其余感官通路，只放行被选中位置的原始信号
临时调高某处感官证据的可信度，让它更能改写所见
向某处加发更多预测，让大脑的猜测压过那里的感官证据
压低某处的预测误差，让那里的信号不再往上层报告
questions.explanation: 在「预期 + 证据，按可靠度加权」的模型里，注意调的是证据的权重（精度）。最诱人的错项把方向说反了：多发预测、压过证据，更接近昏暗中把衣架看成人的那种情形，而不是注意。
questions.question_en: In the predictive processing framework, what is "attention" really doing?
options_en: Shutting down the other sensory channels and letting through only raw signals from the selected location
Briefly raising the trustworthiness of sensory evidence from one place so it can better revise what you see
Sending more predictions to one place so that the brain's guesses override the sensory evidence there
Suppressing prediction error in one place so that signals from there are no longer reported upward
questions.explanation_en: In the model of "expectation + evidence, weighted by reliability," attention adjusts the weight (precision) of the evidence. The most tempting wrong option has the direction backwards: sending more predictions to override evidence is closer to mistaking a coat hanger for a person in the dark than to attention.

questions.question: 伸手去拿杯子，用主动推理的视角看，动作是怎么发生的？
options: 大脑先预测手已握住杯子，这个未实现的预测产生差错，驱动肌肉把它变成真
感知先确认杯子的位置，感知结束后才把结果交给下游的运动系统去执行
大脑先修正信念，承认手还没碰到杯子，再根据新信念规划出一条运动路径
大脑先向肌肉发出运动指令，再用预测去校对手的实际位置是否符合计划
questions.explanation: 预测误差有两种消法：改信念贴合世界，或用动作改世界贴合预测，所以动作是「被身体实现出来的预测」。最诱人的是「先发指令、再校对」，它仍把行动当成感知之外的另一套系统，而主动推理认为两者是同一台机器的两个出口。
questions.question_en: You reach for a cup. From the perspective of active inference, how does the action come about?
options_en: The brain first predicts the hand already holds the cup; this unfulfilled prediction creates an error that drives the muscles to make it true
Perception first confirms where the cup is, and only when it finishes is the result handed to the downstream motor system to execute
The brain first revises its belief, admitting the hand hasn't reached the cup, then plans a movement path based on the new belief
The brain first sends motor commands to the muscles, then uses predictions to check whether the hand's actual position fits the plan
questions.explanation_en: Prediction error can be cancelled in two ways: change beliefs to fit the world, or use action to change the world to fit the prediction; so action is "a prediction fulfilled by the body." The most tempting option is "send commands first, check afterward," which still treats action as a system separate from perception, whereas active inference sees the two as two outlets of the same machine.

questions.question: 家里冰箱的嗡嗡声平时听不见，一停反而立刻警觉。预测加工如何解释这两件事？
options: 大脑判断噪声无关而主动过滤；声音停止是环境变化，触发了本能的危险反应
耳朵对持续刺激逐渐钝化所以听不见；声音停止后敏感度恢复，才察觉异常
声音持续存在时已上报但被高层忽略；声音消失时高层才把注意力调回听觉
声音早被猜中并扣掉，差错为零不上报；它一停预测落空，差错才往上走
questions.explanation: 每层只上报没猜中的部分，熟悉的东西被提前扣掉，「不是耳朵变钝」；反常的是没有声音本身也能引发差错。感官钝化是最诱人的常识解释，但它说不通为什么「没声音」反而让人警觉。
questions.question_en: You normally can't hear the hum of your fridge, yet the moment it stops you're instantly alert. How does predictive processing explain both?
options_en: The brain judges the noise irrelevant and actively filters it out; the stop is an environmental change that triggers an instinctive danger response
Ears gradually dull to a constant stimulus, so you can't hear it; once the sound stops, sensitivity recovers and you notice something's off
While the sound continues it is reported but ignored by higher levels; when it vanishes, those levels turn attention back to hearing
The sound was already predicted and subtracted, so zero error gets reported; when it stops, the prediction fails and error travels upward
questions.explanation_en: Each level reports only what it failed to predict, and familiar things are subtracted in advance: "it's not that your ears got duller." Something out of the ordinary, even the absence of a sound, can itself trigger an error. Sensory dulling is the most tempting common-sense explanation, but it can't explain why "no sound" makes you more alert.
